parts:
Bob etc:  Is this good stuff?  Should we blog it?  Should we have a section in the Stan examples page of user-supplied examples, things we haven't vetted but could still be useful to people?
A

On Nov 27, 2013, at 10:33 PM, Foreman, Kyle wrote:

Hello all,

Attached is a tutorial on taking advantage of sparse precision matrices for multivariate normal likelihoods in Stan. In the case of the Scotland Lip Cancer example (from the GeoBUGS manual) the sparse version is 16x faster than the dense version (for 1000 samples it drops from 195s to 12s).

Sorry for the delay in writing this up - I didn’t have time to set my blog up last week so I figured I’d just put it in a .R file for now.

Best
Kyle

We are having glitches in this model (implementing a detrended second order random walk) and there were some issues in the past related to CAR also.   Implementation aside, there is the speed question for all our autoregressive models. These will be the subject of questions we will likely be asking in the coming weeks so that we can get these models working.

Lea had mentioned the detrended second order random walk but never got back to me with an answer about whether or not the detrending is constant.  In any case we did have
some discussion about possible solutions so it would be productive to find some time to chat about the model and see if we can't implement some of those fixes.
